grader: the Claude Code lane that built this run. NOT a human, and NOT an independent third model. Same weakness the 2026-09-04 pilot recorded, and it points the same way: the lane wrote the seeds, so it knows exactly what a catch looks like, and it is grading a condition that shares its model family.
grading_rules: catch = the review names the seeded defect at its seeded location, or states the wrong behaviour it causes. A finding that merely touches the same function is a miss.
false_findings counts a finding that asserts a defect the code does not have. A finding about a real property of the unmutated code is NOT false, even when it is minor.
A finding that an excluded file is missing (a test file or a doc the case's `paths` filter left out of the diff) is NOT counted as false. The case narrowed the diff, not the reviewer.
These three rules are copied from runs/2026-09-04/grades.json without change, so the two runs are graded by the same standard even though their prompts differ.

VERIFICATION SCOPE, stated rather than implied. Every review was read against its own seeded diff for the seeded defect, which is the catch/miss column. For false_findings this grader checked whether a finding contradicts the seeded diff text on its face; it did NOT independently re-derive every claim a review made about code the seed never touched. A false-finding count of 0 therefore means 'no finding was shown to be false', not 'every finding was proved true'.
